That matters because it suggests rushing usage and a run-game spine that can raise Dart’s fantasy floor while also supporting other Giants skill players. [3]

That’s mostly a team-defense note, but it hints at an aggressive, flexible front that could boost sack and turnover upside. [6]

JAX.summary:
- **Bhayshul Tuten (RB)** — The Jaguars’ most important fantasy battle is at running back, where Tuten and Chris Rodriguez Jr. are in a heated camp competition to replace Travis Etienne’s role. The note says it looks like a timeshare, but Tuten has the narrow edge because of his pass-catching upside, which matters in PPR formats and for Week 1 touch distribution. [2]

- **Brian Thomas Jr. (WR)** — Thomas is being framed as Jacksonville’s best bet to be the WR room’s alpha target, and he’s the only Jaguars receiver included in an ESPN poll of NFL coaches, scouts, and executives ranking the league’s best wideouts. The fantasy angle is straightforward: he’s still the clearest bet on the roster for top-end target volume, even if the article stops short of declaring a true No. 1. [3]

- **Liam Coen (HC)** — Jacksonville finished last season 14th, 6th, and 5th in offense, defense, and special teams DVOA, and Coen retained offensive coordinator Grant Udinski. That points to continuity in the offensive environment, which is a plus for Trevor Lawrence and the passing-game ecosystem even though the exact play-calling split is not specified. [5]

GB.summary:
- **Matthew Golden (WR)** — The discussion around Golden is still centered on whether he can earn targets at the NFL level; this piece pushes back on the “bust” label and says he may not be central to how Green Bay’s offense runs. - **Devonte Wyatt (DT)** — Wyatt is described as Green Bay’s best defensive tackle, but the broader concern is that the Packers’ DT room looks much thinner than the kind of interior group Jonathan Gannon had in Philadelphia.
